full_judgment:
6. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 27.09.2005 dismissed the suit on the finding, inter alia, that the transactions became past and closed long before the insertion of section 95A in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950) and as such, the said section had no manner of application; the plaintiffs failed to prove that their predecessor-in-interest paid back the kabala money and got back possession of the suit land that subsequently, they were dispossessed by the defendants; since the plaintiffs claimed that in payment of the kabala money by their predecessor-in-interest, he got back possession of the suit land, but subsequently, Moniruddin did not execute and register the deed of reconveyance, the suit for redemption was not maintainable and the plaintiffs ought to have filed the suit for specific performance of contact. 

 10. From the facts as emerged from the pleadings of the respective party, it appears that it is an admitted fact that the agreements for reconveyance of the lands of the two kabalas were executed on the same date of the kabalas, i.e. on 11.02.1996 fixing the tenure to repay the kabala money within 4(four) years in respect of kabala No. 1246 and 5 (five) years in respect of kabala No. 1247 and the tenure for repayment of the kabala money in respect of those kabalas expired on 11.02.1971 and 11.02,1972 respectively, i.e. ling before the insertion of section 95A in the Act, 1950 on 03.08.1972 by P.O. 88 of 1972 and the transactions relating to the suit land became past and closed. Therefore, the plaintiffs had no subsisting rights to pray for redemption of the mortgage as prayed for in the suit. This Court in the case of Bangladesh -Vs- Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others, 32DLR (AD) 233; Abdul Khaleque Sarnamat-Vs-Abdul Khaleque Sarnamat and another, 1BLC(AD)90; Abu Bakkar-Vs-Nazir Ahmed, 34 DLR(AD)237 and Mahadeb Chandra Mondol and another-Vs-Dulal Chandra Mondal and others 16 BLT(AD) (2008) 357 clearly held so but the Appellate Court as well as the High Court Division totally misconceived the provisions of section 95A of the Act, 1950 vis-a-vis the facts and circumstances of the case and also failed to apply their mind to the principles of law enunciated by this Court in the above mentioned reported cases in holding that the transactions in question were not hit by the principle of past and closed transactions and thereby fell into an error in decreeing the suit. 

 11. Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam very much relied upon the observation made by this Court in the case of Asmatunnessa and others (supra) to the effect "It may be observed that the learned Judge completely failed to appreciate the provisions of Section 95A of the S.A.T. Act. The Section clearly envisages that a transfer of a holding etc by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding etc. for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the documents relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years to strengthen his submission that the view of the agreement of reconveyance the transactions in question were complete usufructuary mortgage, so after the expiry of 7(seven) years, the plaintiffs were entitled to redeem the same in view of the provisions of section 95A of the Act." The quoted observations made by this Court in the above cited case do not help Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam inasmuch as in the reported case, the registered deed and the Ekrarnama, it was stipulated that the land would be reconveyed if the kabala. money amounting to taka 400.00 (four hundred) was returned within four years and this four years would end on 22.10.1974, whereas section 95A was inserted in Act, 1950 by P.0.88 of 1972 on 03.08.1972, so by no stretch of imagination, it could be said that the transaction involved in the reported case (Asmatunnessa and others) became a past and closed one before the insertion of section 95A in the Act. Moreso, in the reported case, the question of past and closed transaction was not at all raised and decided. It also needs to be mentioned that in the reported case, this Court also observed that "the facts of the instant case fully answer the above description and it is clear that the transaction thus qualified to be a complete usufructuary mortgage by operation of law."
